items.sum: Postoperative drops create adherence, instillation, ocular-surface toxicity, and cost burdens.  Dropless cataract surgery transfers medication delivery to surgery but comprises heterogeneous techniques and evidence.

items.t: Gender disparities in cataract-related blindness and visual impairment: analysis of data from 204 countries
items.sum: Gender disparities exist in cataract-related vision loss, with variations across regions. Lower literacy rates, lower health expenditures, and a higher burden of cataract-blindness were associated with such disparities. Key points: Although cataract blindness declined globally by 32.2% between 1990 and 2019, gender disparities in cataract-related vision loss have persisted, and in some regions, worsened. The highest disparities were observed in South Asia…

items.t: Optimal target offset under asymmetric refractive loss and discrete intraocular lens power steps
items.src: Journal of Cataract and Refractive Surgery
items.sum: Slight myopia is often chosen during intraocular lens power selection to avoid a hyperopic result, but the appropriate offset depends on prediction uncertainty and the consequences of residual refraction.  This analysis derived the target that minimizes expected loss under unequal penalties for myopic and hyperopic outcomes and assessed discrete lens choices.

items.t: From area under the curve to clinical readiness: A framework for AI-assisted ectasia risk assessment before refractive surgery
items.sum: Artificial intelligence (AI) models for keratoconus frequently report near-perfect discrimination, with pooled sensitivity and specificity approaching 98% when manifest keratoconus is separated from normal corneas.  These figures are increasingly invoked to answer a different, more consequential question: whether an apparently non-ectatic cornea can safely undergo refractive surgery.
